J1_line_asserts_challenged_proposition.justification: The response challenges 'The inequality \sum_{i=1}^{r}(5n/2-3i)-3r+\lfloor (n-3r)^2/4\rfloor \le \lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor stated in line 0017 is false.' First-choice line 17 is precisely 'However, one can show that $$\sum_{i=1}^{r}(\frac{5n}{2}-3i)-3r+\lfloor\frac{(n-3r)^2}{4}\rfloor\leq\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\rfloor,$$'. Its active assumptions are line 5-6 (G on n vertices with floor(n^2/4)+1 edges), line 8 (r is the size of a maximal system of vertex-disjoint triangles, so that deleting those 3r vertices leaves a triangle-free graph) and the contradiction hypothesis of line 12; the displayed inequality itself involves only n and r.

J2_evidence_specified.justification: 'For n=10 and r=1 the left side equals 31 while the right side equals 25, violating the inequality.' Both parameters and both numerical values are given, and the response's own derivation shows the algebra (5nr/2 - 3r(r+3)/2 + floor((n-3r)^2/4)).

J3_evidence_check.justification: Recomputed exactly in rational arithmetic (scripts/P22_check.py). For n=10, r=1: sum_{i=1}^{1}(5n/2-3i) = 25-3 = 22, minus 3r gives 19, plus floor((10-3)^2/4) = 12 gives 31, while floor(10^2/4) = 25; 31 > 25, so line 17's inequality fails at the witness. The parameter pair is admissible under the source's assumptions, which I also checked rather than assumed: the script builds a 10-vertex graph with exactly floor(n^2/4)+1 = 26 edges (triangle {a,b,c}, a triangle-free K_{3,4} on the other seven vertices, and 11 edges joining them) in which {a,b,c} is a triangle and G-{a,b,c} contains no triangle at all, so {a,b,c} is a maximal system of vertex-disjoint triangles with r = 1 exactly as line 8 requires. The supplied evidence therefore refutes the located assertion. (The script also shows the inequality failing at several other (n,r); the reading rests on the supplied n=10, r=1.)

J4_consequence_overreach.justification: The response states only that the line-17 inequality is false, with the numeric witness. It does not go on to claim that the Statement of lines 5-6, Erdos's lemma, or the surrounding argument is false; its own deliberation in fact concludes the statement itself is true ('So the statement is actually true. So maybe false assertion is elsewhere').
